Fire Fighting Sectional Committee, CED 22 


FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Fire Fighting 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 


Hazmat-cum-Rescue Appliance is designed and fabricated so as to provide facilities necessary to deal with the 
emergent situations arising due to accidents involving fire, chemicals, road/rail accidents, building collapse and 
similar other situations caused by man made and natural calamities and to provide data and communication 
support with the aid of computers and other fail-proof satellite-linked communication equipment for efficient 
rescue operations at the accident site. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised) . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16095 : 2013 


Indian Standard 
HAZMAT VEHICLE — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard lays down the requirements regarding 
material, design and construction, workmanship and 
finish, accessories and equipments of Hazmat vehicle 
for fire brigade use. 


2 DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION 


2.1 Chassis 


The chassis for the appliance shall be selected such as 
meeting national norms on safety, emission, etc, while 
providing ample space for carrying the equipment as 
per given in Annex A and other facilities stipulated in 
this standard. The engine shall have sufficient power 
so as to meet road performance standards for such class 
of emergency appliance when fully laden. The vehicle 
should be right hand drive and all the manoeuvrings 
systems shall be power assisted. 


2.2 Driver’s and Crew Cab 


a) Type — Semi-forward control type, designed 
for a crew of 6 (one driver + one Incident 
commander and four fireman). 

b) Design — The driver’s cab shall be rigid 
safety cell with well tuned suspension and 
ensuring comfort almost equal to that of a 
passenger car. Design shall offer excellent all 
round vision. The cab shall be adequately 
insulated against noise, vibration and extreme 


temperatures. 

c) Doors — Two doors, with roll down 
windows. 

d) Windshield — Safety glass or custom built, 
if desired. 


e) Seats — One driver’s seat adjustable type, one 
centre seat and one co-driver’s seat. 


f) Dashboard — The dashboard shall be 
equipped with all necessary gauges, pilot 
lamps and switches. 


g) Control Panel — It shall be located on the 
dashboard between the driver’s and co- 
driver’s seat. This panel shall comprise, 


1) pilot lamp doors open/closed; 

2) pilot lamp rotating beacons on/off; 

3) windshield wipers and washers; 

4) cab interior illumination; 

5) heating and ventilation unit, defroster; 


6) two rear view mirrors; 

7) two sun visors; and 

8) an air-conditioning system for the cabin. 
To prevent toxic gases coming into the cabin, a 
circulating air filter system with air condition shall be 
provided behind the cabin. The whole system shall 
consist of housing, a radial fan, filter unit, air 
conditioner and the operating unit. 


2.3 Circulating Air Filter System 


a) Housing — The housing shall be made of 
steel. It shall be insulated against noise and 
heat. 

b) Double High Pressure Radial Fan — The fan 
delivers the toxic gas from outside to the filter 
unit. Furthermore, it recirculates the used air 
in the working room. 

c) Voltage — 24 V. 

d) Revolutions — 8 500/min. 

e) Operation Temperature — —30°C to + 60°C 

f) Filter Unit — The whole unit shall consist of 
a fresh air filter, a circulating air filter and an 
activated carbon filter. 

g) Operating Unit — Mounted in the cabin, with 
all necessary gauges and control lamps. 


2.4 Bodywork in General 


a) Construction — The superstructure shall 
consist of four main compartments, namely 
working room with a small locker 
compartment, pump compartment, tank and 
decontamination cell. The vehicle shall be 
designed in such a manner that right side of 
compartment shall be integrated type which 
will be hydraulically operated (single 
compartment shall be used for rain, sunlight 
protection; provision for shed). 

b) Ladder — Two foldable aluminium ladders, 
one on each side, mounted in the rear of the 
vehicle, to give access to the working deck 
of the vehicle. 

c) Roof — Covered with aluminium chequered 
plate above the working room and the 
decontamination cell. Above the tank and 
pump compartment, removable grids shall be 
provided. The deck rail shall be made of light 
alloy. 


IS 16095 : 2013 


2.5 Working Room and Locker Compartment 


The superstructure shall be made of steel lightweight 
hollow profiles with light alloy panelling. The working 
room shall have provision to enter from the L/H side 
of the vehicle via a swing out door. Automatic swing 
out doorsteps and ergonomically mounted handgrips 
facilitate an easy access and exit. Two fixed windows, 
one on the L/H side and one on the R/H side shall be 
provided for good illumination of the room. The door 
shall also be provided with a small window. 


The cabin should normally be provided with a table, 
chair, a shelving rack, a small cabinet, a computer 
system with printer, a telefax machine, a mobile 
telephone, GPS linkage and radio installation. Due to 
safety and transportation the rotatary chair shall be 
fixed on the floor. The computer system shall be 
provided with a colour monitor and a black/white 
printer. For the camera mounted onto the light mast, a 
black/white monitor shall be also provided inside the 
room. The cabinet shall be provided with drawers. The 
roof shall be covered with aluminium chequered plates 
and shall be walked on. Working room shall be air 
conditioned including equipment for communication. 


One locker compartment shall be directly mounted 
behind the step for the working room, only on the L/H 
side. The storage locker shall be closed by a dust and 
water proof light-alloy roller shutter, provided with a 
lock. The dual-skinned design roller shutter shall 
always be opened even if a tool comes off its bracket 
which normally blocks the roller shutters. The profiles 
shall be embedded in a special type of plastic material, 
extremely low on noise, and smooth running. 


Illumination — Automatic, when opening the roller 
shutters, with yellow pilot light on the control panel in 
the driver’s cab. 


2.6 Pump Compartment 


The pump compartment shall be located directly behind 
the working room. It shall be closed by two dust and 
water proof light alloy roller shutter on each side, 
provided with a lock. The dual skinned design roller 
shutter shall always be opened even, if a tool comes 
off its bracket, which normally blocks the roller 
shutters. The profiles shall be embedded in a special 
type of plastic material, extremely low on noise, and 
smooth running. 


Illumination — Automatic, when opening the roller 
shutters, with yellow pilot light on the control panel in 
the driver’s cab. 


2.7 Decontamination Room 


The decontamination room shall be made of steel 
profile tubes, with light alloy panelling. The room shall 


be mounted behind the tank. The decontamination room 
shall have provision to enter from the rear of the vehicle 
via hydraulic loading platform. The decontamination 
cell shall be equipped with a high pressure cleaning 
unit with two water inlets and one water recycling unit 
for the waste water. 


The dashboard, mounted in the storage locker shall be 
illuminated and equipped with switches for the HP- 
cleaning unit and the diving pump (necessary for the 
water recycling unit). In case of biological and 
radiological contamination, the decontaminated water 
to be contained in an enclosed safe packet. 


2.8 Hydraulic Loading Platform 


a) Payload — 500 kg 
b) Drive — Electro/hydraulically 
c) Voltage — 24 V 


3 PUMP UNIT LOCATION: MIDSHIP 


3.1 Centrifugal Pump 


a) Design — Combined normal and high 
pressure pump. Arrangement of one normal 
pressure stage and one high pressure stages. 

b) Material — Pump housing and impeller shall 
be made of corrosion-resistant gun-metal and 
the pump shaft shall be made of stainless steel. 

c) Pump Output — 4 000 l/min at 1 MPa 

400 l/min at 4 MPa (valid 
during tank suction 
operation) 


d) Water Pipe Work — Carbonized steel, hot dip 
galvanized. 


e) Foam Compound Pipe Work — Stainless steel 
or PVC. 


3.2 Priming Device 


a) Design — The piston priming pump which is 
mounted on top of the gearbox shall be driven 
via a V-belt. A lever shall tighten the V-belt 
via a tension pulley and open and closes the 
ball valve respectively for the suction line. As 
soon as the pump discharges water and a 
pressure of approximately 0.15 MPa is reached, 
a hydraulic cylinder controls the tension pulley 
automatically. By means of a hand lever which 
is connected to the tension pulley the priming 
pump shall be disengaged manually, that is in 
case of pump operation in idling speed or when 
working with lowest pressure. 

b) Material — The casing and piston are made 
of light alloy and the cylinder box of stainless 
steel. 


3.3 Piping 


a) Pressure Outlets — 4 Nos. Normal pressure 


outlets, 63 mm couplings. 
1 No. Normal pressure 
outlet connected to the 
normal pressure hose 
reel. 

2 Nos. High pressure 
outlets 25 mm, one 
connected to the high 
pressure hose reel, one 
on the L/H side of the 
vehicle. 


1 No. Tank filling line. 


1 No. Normal pressure 
line for the monitor. 


b) Suction Inlets — 1 No. Suction inlet with 


coupling, on the R/H side. 
1 No. Water tank suction 
connection. 

1 No. External foam 
suction connection. 

1 No. Foam tank suction 
connection. 


c) Drain Valves — For pump and foam system. 


3.4 Pump Control Panel 


a) Location — On the R/H side of the vehicle. 
b) Actuations for — Control panel illumination. 


Water tank suction valve. 
Water tank filling via pump. 


Piston priming pump. 
High pressure outlets. 


Selector switch for foam 
admixing ratio 3 percent or 
6 percent. 


c) Indicators — Water tank level indicator. 


3.5 Water Tank 


Foam tank level indicator. 
Normal pressure manometer. 
High pressure manometer. 
Mano-vacuummeter. 
Working hour meter. 
Cooling water temperature 
gauge. 

Control lights: PTO engaged. 


Oil pressure drive engine. 
Foam operation. 


a) Capacity — 1 000 litre. 
b) Construction — Mounted between pump

3.7 Normal Pressure Hose Reel Installation 


a) 


b) 


c) 


Design — One hose reel, mounted in the 
pump locker on the R/H side, for use with 
normal pressure water or foam. The reel shall 
be fitted with a reliable drum brake and an 
electric rewinding of the rubber hose. The reel 
shall be of the swivel type, hinged forward 
45°, for easy unwinding of the hose. This 
facilitates and speeds up operations by the 
ground crew. For maintenance purposes, the 
reels shall be swivelled 90°, allowing for 
better accessibility to the pump room. 

Hose — The hose reel holds 30 m of rubber 
hose of 32 mm internal diameter. 


Foam Branch — The end of the hose shall be 
fitted with a normal pressure fog gun, output 


IS 16095 : 2013 


of 200 l/min at 1 MPa. A foam branch pipe 
shall be provided with the vehicle. 


3.8 High Pressure Hose Reel Installation 


a) 


b) 


c) 


Design — One hose reel, mounted in the pump 
locker on the L/H side, for use with high 
pressure water or foam. The reel shall be fitted 
with a reliable drum brake, and an electric 
rewinding of the rubber hose. The reel shall 
be of the swivel type, hinged forward 45°, for 
easy unwinding of the hose. This facilitates 
and speeds up operations by the ground crew. 
For maintenance purposes, the reels shall be 
swivelled 90°, allowing for better accessibility 
to the pump room. 

Hose — The hose reel shall be of 60 m of 
rubber hose 25 mm internal diameter. 

Foam Branch — The end of the hose shall be 
fitted with a normal pressure fog gun, output 
200 l/min at 4 MPa. A high pressure foam 
branch pipe shall be provided with the vehicle.

30. | Breathing apparatus with air cylinder 6.8 1/30 MPa 


Positive pressure type, consisting of, 


a) Light-weight positive pressure face mask — Injection moulded liquid silicone outer mask, 
thermoplastic elastomer (TPE) inner mask and an impact and scratch resistant double 
curvature visor with double coating. Low profile, quick lock, bayonet demand valve 
connection, integral spectacle frame mounting and superior speech reproduction. Compact 
Low Profile Demand Valve with new lower pressure first breath mechanism and hand-free 
true bypass. The servo-assisted design to provide excellent breathing performance. 

b) Gauge and whistle — The gauge having a photo-luminescent gauge face and placed in a 
stainless steel case with rubber shroud. Provided with a shatterproof poly-carbonate lens 
and shoulder mounted for easy reference. 

c) Light-weight ergonomic back plate and harness — Anti-static moulded composite back 
plate, Kevlar cylinder band, and fully adjustable, flame retardant harness with lumbar pad 
for long term comfort. 


Supply Hoses are fixed by U-clip swivel and O-ring seals for easy maintenance. They have 
different diameter connections for fool-proof assembly. 

d) Pressure reducing valve — It shall be a fail-safe piston type valve with a safety pressure 6 
relief valve. An internal restrictor protects gauge and whistle from air-loss. Low 
maintenance. Cylinders come complete with one carbon fully wrapped composite air 
cylinder 6.8 1/30 MPa (50 min nominal duration). 


e) Attachment options — Decontamination attachments, RSM attachment for resuscitator/ 
rescue mask, Airline attachment for extended working, Quick-fill attachment

34. | Right angle safety torch — This torch design and construction shall be of the highest standards 
of safety and reliability. It shall be made from a tough anti-static plastic material and all metal 
parts of non-ferrous. Beside its safety features, it shall be also completely water and dust proof. 


Colour: yellow. 
Temperature class T6. 
Complete with 2 round dry cell batteries R 20, 1.5 V and 2 spare bulbs. 

35.| Airline system trolley — Designed for restricted-access operations for up to two breathing 
apparatus wearers, the system consists of a hose reel unit and a cylinder frame used either 
together or separately. Each cylinder frame is designed to carry a pair of cylinders and features 
an adjustable cylinder band to allow the use of various cylinder sizes. Where required, cylinder 
frames may be stacked to increase capacity to four cylinders. The high-pressure cylinder 
connections may be used with either 20 or 30 MPa cylinders and feature non-return bleed 
valves to facilitate the replacement of one cylinder while another one is still in use. The high 
pressure 30 MPa regulator may deliver up to 1 000 l/min of breathing air and is fitted with both 
high and medium-pressure gauges and a high-pressure warning whistle. 


The system is fitted with wheels and a handle for easy transport. Both may be removed if 
required. Comes with two cylinders 6 1/30 MPa, made of steel. 


Stainless steel tubular frame, fixed in fully adjustable cylinder bands high pressure pneumatic 

system with 5.5 MPa while 20/30 MPa with outlet coupling. The hose reel fitted with 60 m of 

10 mm bore antistatic hose. 

a) Y-Piece assembly with couplings to separate main compressor airline supply into two 
branch lines 


b) Delivery hose 10 m including fittings for connection of Y-Piece of the airline system to the 
flit system 


36. | Airline escape breathing apparatus — Comprising a positive pressure face mask in black 
neoprene, an automatic positive pressure demand valve, a supply hose and a pigtail with

54. | Portable decontamination shower — Major decontamination shower “Suitcase’ type with dual 
purpose foot platform/carrying case, lightweight and compact. Assembly time: less than 30 s. 
necessity for a heavy duty stainless steel tubular base. Instead the base design is a lay flat hose 


The extremely rugged carrying case duals as a most effective base platform, eliminating the 
assembly, providing resultant cost and weight savings. The 40 mm lay flat duraline hoses form 
four shower legs, each of which is fitted with four spray nozzles. The base hose assembly 
which fits around the foot platform incorporates four 40 mm male instantaneous couplings 
which mate with the female couplings on the legs. When under pressure, all the hose legs and 
the base hose assembly become rigid, thus forming a stable frame for decontamination of 
personnel, complete with non slip raised platform. 

55.|Inflatable decontamination shelter — For containment of contaminated water. Shelter frame 
incorporates four legs which are inflated under low pressure. The four supporting legs are 
sheeted on all sides with two opposite sides incorporating windows to enable those assisting to 
observe the decontamination process. With openings the other two opposite sides to enable 
personnel to walk-through from a dirty area to a clean area. Openings fitted with drop down 
splash flaps to prevent contaminated water splashing into surrounding area. Inlet and outlet 
trunks are located in the heavy duty floor. Dimension of inlet and outlet 40 mm.

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CED 22 (7609).
